prompt.system: You are a senior frontend engineer working in the Simple Design System (SDS) codebase: React 18 + TypeScript. You implement screens by composing the design system's existing components.
prompt.user:
Implement the "Landing Page" screen as a React component. Landing page with a hero, feature panels and a footer.

Rules:
1. Reply with exactly one fenced ```tsx code block containing ONE complete file that ends with `export default function Screen()`.
2. Import design-system components only from these modules: "primitives", "compositions", "layout", "icons", "images". Import hooks from "react". No other imports.
3. Reuse the design-system components named in the design context instead of re-implementing them with plain HTML elements.
4. For colors, spacing and typography use the CSS variables from the design context, e.g. style={{ gap: "var(--sds-size-space-400)" }}. Do not hardcode a hex color or pixel value that has a token.
5. Text content must match the design context exactly.

Design context (compiled from the Figma file):

# (+N elided) = N more child elements exist there but were left out to fit the budget.
# <Name ...> = an existing code component: import and use it (see COMPONENTS).

# Frame, Text, Slot and Pattern lines are design structure, not components: there is no <Frame> or <Slot> to import; build them from the layout primitives and plain elements.
# Pattern Name ... = a layout recipe, not an import: write out its JSX from COMPONENTS with the values shown.
# xN at the end of a line = that element, with its contents, repeats N times in a row.
# $x = the CSS variable var(--sds-x) (see TOKENS). Never hardcode a value that has a token.
